name: Death and the Intermediate State
path: Eschatology: The Doctrine of Last Things

objectives.text: Identify from the Bible that every person will die one day
Name the Bible's teaching that believers go to be with Jesus when they die
Explain from Genesis and Romans that death entered the world because of sin
Retell Jesus' words to Martha that whoever believes in him will live even though he dies
Describe how Paul says Christians grieve at death differently from those who have no hope
Explain what Paul means when he says Jesus has taken away the sting of death
Summarize the Westminster Shorter Catechism's answer about what believers receive from Christ at death
Explain the Heidelberg Catechism's answer to why believers still die even though Christ died for them
Explain that Scripture describes death as the separation of the soul from the body
Explain how Psalm 90 teaches God's people to number their days in light of death
Explain why Paul considers departing to be with Christ far better than remaining in the body
Compare the state of the righteous and the wicked immediately after death as taught in Scripture and the Westminster Confession
Interpret Jesus' promise to the thief on the cross in its context to show that believers are with Christ immediately at death
Explain how the Reformed practice of Christian burial reflects the teaching that believers' bodies remain united to Christ as they rest in the grave
Analyze New Testament passages that portray departed souls as conscious and active before the resurrection
Explain from Scripture why a person's eternal destiny is fixed at death with no second chance afterward
Explain why the intermediate state is not the believer's final hope by connecting the disembodied soul to the future resurrection of the body
Explain from Scripture why God forbids attempts to contact or consult the dead
Analyze Old Testament language about Sheol and being gathered to one's people to trace how the hope beyond death unfolds across Scripture
Evaluate the doctrine of soul sleep against Scripture by interpreting the biblical metaphor of death as sleep
Evaluate the Roman Catholic doctrine of purgatory against Scripture and the Reformed confessions
Compose a theological essay on death and the intermediate state that integrates the key passages and confessional statements and distinguishes the intermediate state from the final state

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (death is universal, believers with Jesus, sting of death removed, WSC Q37 summary, believer vs unbeliever, Philippians 1, the thief on the cross, intermediate state not final hope, soul sleep and purgatory). Split the combined grade 11 evaluation into separate soul sleep and purgatory objectives, and turned the soul-sleep item into an interpretation of the sleep metaphor. Folded 'connect to future resurrection' and 'analyze the soul apart from the body' into the grade 9 and grade 8 objectives, and merged 'construct a theology' and 'synthesize the hope' into one grade 12 capstone. Dropped 'defend conscious existence' as covered by the grade 8 analysis and the soul sleep evaluation. Reframed 'apply the comfort' as explaining Paul's reasoning so no objective targets a student's feelings. Added death as the result of sin, John 11:25-26, grieving with hope, Heidelberg Q42 on why believers die, death as soul-body separation, numbering our days, Christian burial, no change of destiny after death, the prohibition on consulting the dead, and Old Testament Sheol language. Added WCF 32.1, Heidelberg Q42 and Q57, and WSC Q19 as anchors.
